testCases.name: test_case_2
testCases.input: What is positional encoding and why is it needed?
testCases.actualOutput:
According to Paper: Attention Is All You Need, "the Transformer uses sinusoidal positional encodings" (Table 1 row (C) is not explicitly mentioned but a similar sentence can be found in another section of the paper).

In the context of this paper, Positional Encoding refers to a technique used to help the model understand the order and relative position of elements in the input sequence.

The need for positional encoding arises from the fact that the attention mechanism only considers relative positions between different parts of the input sequence. In other words, it is not possible to directly compute "where is the first element in relation to any given other element". 

This limitation means that the model would have difficulty understanding long-range dependencies and relationships within a sequence.

To address this challenge, an additional set of parameters, the positional encoding vector PE(pos), is added to each position (pos) in the input sequence. This allows the attention mechanism to consider both absolute positions and relative positions between different parts of the sequence.

testCases.name: test_case_4
testCases.input: How does scaled dot-product attention work?
testCases.actualOutput:
According to Paper: Attention Is All You Need, scaled dot-product attention is a mechanism used for self-attention and query-key-value attention. It works as follows:

1. The input sequence is first split into three matrices: Q (query), K (key), and V (value).
2. These matrices are computed by taking the position-wise attention (self-attention) of each element in the input sequence.
3. The scaled dot-product attention computes the output matrix using the formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q * K^T / sqrt(dk))
4. The softmax function is used to compute the weights for each pair of elements from Q and K.

The key point here is that scaled dot-product attention masks out (sets to 0) all values in the input of the softmax corresponding to illegal connections, i.e., positions in the previous layer of the encoder or decoder. This is done to prevent leftward information flow and preserve the auto-regressive property.

Source: [Paper: Attention Is All You Need]
